beats.narration: Here is a curve, and one point on it, where x equals one. How steep is the curve right at that point? A slope needs two points, and we only have one.
So take a second point, two units to the right. Draw the line through both points. It rises two while it runs two, so its slope is exactly one.
Now slide the second point toward the first. Watch the slope as the gap shrinks: it falls, and settles on one half. The line has become the tangent, the line that just touches the curve at our point.
That limit is the derivative. Take the slope over a gap h, then let h shrink to zero. At x equals one, the derivative of this curve is one half.
